newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-L.A. Dodgers join new football stadium campaign.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-L.A. Dodgers join new football stadium campaign.

text.p: The president of the Los Angeles Dodgers baseball team said on Monday he would support a $150 million plus plan to build a new stadium at the site of the landmark Coliseum to attract a professional football team.
"The Dodgers will join you in supporting a new stadium at the Coliseum site," said Dodgers President Peter O'Malley in a letter to a Los Angeles City councilman.

Under the proposal, a $150 million plus stadium would be built within the Coliseum's existing walls. The facility would have a seating capacity of 67,000, a middle deck with about 140 luxury suites and an additional 8,000 club seats.
Decisions have yet been made on methods of financing.

The announcement that the Dodgers organization has joined the Coliseum campaign should provide a "boost to our effort to create a 'Sports and Entertainment Corridor,'" said Los Angeles City Councilman Mark Ridley-Thomas, chair of the council's ad hoc committee on sports.
O'Malley expressed his support for the Coliseum plan in a letter to Ridley-Thomas.

"The National Football League has consistently expressed a desire to work with Los Angeles in placing a team in this market once it can be assured of the long-term viability of that franchise," O'Malley said in the letter. "That viability is critically dependent on the development of a new, state-of-the-art professional football venue."
